Classical Fermat criterion identifies interior junction iff every angle<120°, otherwise a sampled angle>=120° is the minimizing hub. The maximum C−A for x>=−a,z<=a is 2 arctan(a), attained only at boundary x=−a,y=0,z=a, yielding a0=1/sqrt3. Maximizing left-end angle over x=−r,y→x,z=a produces F(r,a)=atan(a−r)+atan(2r); differentiating its exact threshold inequality yields unique tangent-contact a1=sqrt3/2+2sqrt6/3 at r=(1/2+sqrt2)/sqrt3; reflection gives right-end. At each unique extremizer the event condition has two linearly shrinking positive endpoint deficits and one quadratically shrinking central variable, hence δ^(5/2) Jacobian. Taylor normal forms give D0: u+w+(sqrt3/2)v²<2, D1: u/2+w+sqrt(3/2)v²<1. Direct integration gives volumes 64/(15*3^(1/4)) and 16/(15*(3/2)^(1/4)); multiplying ordered uniform-triple density 3/(4a³), and both endpoint labels, yields the two reported sharp coefficients. Compact localization around unique strict maxima and normalized indicator L1 convergence prove conditional total variation; numerical small-δ tests only corroborate.
